notes.meaning: The speaker pledges never to be silent or take ease until Jerusalem's righteousness and salvation burst forth like the morning sun or a blazing torch. This tireless speaking and praying will continue until God's promises of rescue are fully carried out. It shows how deeply God's servants and the Lord himself care for the spiritual good of his people.

When the Lord restores his people, foreign nations and their rulers will witness the splendor and goodness God has given them. The Lord himself will give his people a brand new name, marking their changed condition from shame to honor. A name given by God shows that their new identity and value are real and permanent.

God's people are described as a glorious crown and a royal diadem held safely in the hand of the Lord. Instead of wearing the crown on his head, the Lord displays it in his palm to show how precious his people are to him. Being held in his hand means they are treasured, cared for, and kept under his constant protection.

The people and their homeland will no longer be known as abandoned or ruined, names that once matched their painful time in exile. Instead, the Lord will call them Hephzibah, which means 'my delight is in her,' and Beulah, which means 'married.' God promises to take deep pleasure in his people and to restore their land so it is filled with life once again.

Just as a young bridegroom feels great happiness on his wedding day, so God will rejoice with gladness over his people. In a similar way, the citizens of the land will pledge themselves to their home, settling down to love and care for it. God's affection for his people is not a cold duty, but a warm and active joy.

The Lord places faithful watchmen upon the city walls who stay alert and speak out continuously, day and night. These praying servants are told to give themselves no rest, and to give God no rest, until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it praised across the earth. God warmly invites his people to be bold and persistent in prayer, reminding him of what he has promised.

The Lord makes a solemn oath by his own strength that enemies will never again steal the harvest his people worked so hard to grow. Those who gather the grain and grapes will eat and drink their own food in peace, worshiping the Lord with gratitude in his sacred temple courts. When God provides for our needs, we can gladly enjoy his gifts and honor him with thankful hearts.

A call goes out to pass through the city gates and clear the road so the returning people can travel freely. Workers are told to build up a smooth highway, clear away every stumbling stone, and lift up a banner high in the air as a rallying point. This picture pointed to captives marching out of Babylon, and also shows the way being prepared for people to come to God's salvation.

The Lord announces good news to the farthest parts of the earth, telling his people that their Savior is coming. He arrives with full power, bringing peace, comfort, and a lasting reward for his faithful servants. This worldwide announcement points forward to the good news of Jesus being preached to all nations.

The people will receive honorable titles: they will be called the Holy People and the Redeemed of the Lord, showing that God has paid the price to rescue and sanctify them. Jerusalem itself will be called 'Sought Out' and 'A City Not Forsaken,' because God and travelers will once again cherish and visit it. Those who belong to the Lord will never be abandoned or forgotten.
